issue_context.title: Print message after codespace delete
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

Currently once the codespace is deleted the command does not print any message after successful deletion. It would be nice if the `gh cs delete` command prints a message after successfully deletion of one or more than one codespace.

### Proposed solution

If a single codespace is deleted then show codespace display name
`Successfully deleted cli/cli (trunk): refactored adventure`

Edit: Alternatively we can do
`Successfully deleted kousikmitra-refactored-adventure-abc123xyz`

If multiple codespace is delete then show a count of deleted codespaces.
`Successfully deleted 5 codespaces"

### Additional context
NA

Add any other context like screenshots or mockups are helpful, if applicable.
NA
comments:
Not a bad idea, thanks! I like especially in the case of deleting multiple codespaces to print out the number of deleted codespaces.

The confirmation message should be added after this block, and only if stout is connected to a terminal https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/350011162a66810b8515886cddea9ec1cfac49d8/pkg/cmd/codespace/delete.go#L172

/cc @cli/codespaces

review_comments: This isn't your change, but I wonder if we shouldn't return the `err` here - the `errgroup.Wait` will return the first time that it sees an error, so it may either not attempt to delete all the codespaces, or it may exit event with some goroutines will running. Since we're already printing the error message, we could just `return nil` even if deletion fails just to ensure that all the deletes are attempted and complete
Will need to check on this, I will get back.

```
func (*errgroup.Group).Wait() error
Wait blocks until all function calls from the Go method have returned, then returns the first non-nil error (if any) from them.
```
It waits until all go routine has finished.
Ahh good to know 😄 looks good then

What do you think about modifying the message if it was a partial-success scenario and some failed to delete (in other words if `deletedCodespaces < len(codespacesToDelete)`? The failure messages will already be printed to stderr, but I think having a message at the end with a check mark and a "success" message might be misleading.

I would propose the following:
* If all deleted successfully, use the messages you have currently
* If `deletedCodespaces > 0 && deletedCodespaces < len(codespacesToDelete)`, print out `fmt.Sprintf("%s %d codespaces deleted successfully, but %d codespaces failed to delete\n", cs.WarningIcon(), deletedCodespaces, len(codespacesToDelete) - deletedCodespaces)`

I *think* that the message that some codespaces failed to delete is already printed out, because on line 189 we'll return an error saying as much. I wonder if we should have that error specify the exact number so that the messaging is cleaner. Either way, it looks like if there is an error we would currently write `Successfully deleted <n> codespaces` to `stdout` and `some codespaces failed to delete` to `stderr` which is a bit redundant

@cmbrose yes, but I find it confusing if the message on `stdout` makes it sound like everything was successful. I'd rather it print a warning in this case since there was some success and some failure. The exact details of the failures are written to `stderr` already.

@jkeech yeah I wasn't disagreeing with you, just saying that whatever the messaging ends up being we should look at what the entire output looks like and see if it makes sense. I think that if there's an error, the output would look something like this (assume 1 codespace successfully deletes and one fails):

```
error deleting codespace "abcd": an error message
1 codespaces deleted successfully, but 1 codespaces failed to delete
some codespaces failed to delete
```

There's a lot of redundancy there, it seems like it would be a good time to clean it up.

True, wondering if we should print to stdout only in case the command is successful else in case of error or partial success print to stderr? Maybe replace `some codespaces failed to delete` with `successfully deleted 1 codespace, but failed to delete 1`

It's going to be hard to get totally rid of the final `some codespaces failed to delete` message because that is coming from `return err` which is something that we don't want to remove. Given that, make we use separate messages to specify success and delete count - some example cases:

All deletes succeed:
```
<n> codespace(s) deleted successfully
```

Mixed success:
```
error deleting codespace "abcd": an error message
<n> codespace(s) deleted successfully
<m> codespace(s) failed to delete
```

All deletes fail:
```
error deleting codespace "abcd": an error message
<m> codespace(s) failed to delete
```

We should be able to do that pretty easily with the current code - just update the error message on 189 and keep this success message as currently written
yes this will bee fairly easy, will make the change.
